::: {.callout-important}
## Status
This variable dictionary is a working draft. Confirm the final variable
list, value-label codes, and the precise definition of `welfare_self` with the 50by35 methodology team before treating it as authoritative.
:::

## Overview

Every harmonized file uploaded and approved through the pipeline must conform to this schema. Variables are grouped into **mandatory** (must be present and non-missing per the rules of the variable) and **optional** (included when available in the source survey).

The **unit of observation** is the individual: one row per person, with household-level variables (e.g. `welfare`, `hhid`) repeated across all members of the same household.

**File-level requirements** (in addition to the variable rules below):

- **One survey per file.** `code`, `year` and `survname` have the same value in every row (checked by the validators). The upload scripts read them from the first row to look up CPI/PPP.
- **Refugee sample only.** The file contains the 50by35 monitoring population (see [Harmonize Data](02-harmonization.qmd)), with weights for that population.
- **File name** is `<survey ID>_WELF.dta`, for example `COL_2023_GEIH_V01_M_V01_A_FDP_WELF.dta`.
- **Every mandatory variable is a column in the file**, even where its values may be missing (see `camp` and `urban`).

## Conventions

- **Type** refers to the recommended Stata storage type of the variable in the
  harmonized `.dta` file: `str#` (string), `byte`/`int`/`long` (integers),
  `double` (reals). Integer types are interchangeable: running `compress`
  before saving may store an integer variable in a smaller type, which is
  accepted. Real-valued variables (`welfare`, `welfare_self`, `weight`, `age`,
  `natpovline`) must not be stored as `float`, which keeps only about 7
  significant digits; `compress` never converts `double` to `float`, but may
  store integer-valued reals as `byte`/`int`/`long`, which is accepted.
  Storage types are checked only by the Stata validator, because
  [`haven`](https://haven.tidyverse.org) reads every Stata numeric into R as
  `double`; the R validator checks values only.
- **Missing** — mandatory variables may not be missing except where noted. Use
  Stata's system missing (`.`) for genuinely unknown values; do not use numeric
  sentinels such as `-9` or `99`, or extended missing values (`.a`–`.z`).
- **Labels** — categorical variables must carry Stata value labels; the numeric
  codes below are authoritative and must match across all surveys. Every
  variable should carry the text in the **Label** column as its Stata variable
  label (`label variable`), with units in brackets where applicable; the
  validators warn when a label differs.
- **Identifiers** are strings to preserve leading zeros and avoid precision loss.

## Mandatory Variables

| Variable | Label | Type | Unit / range | Missing | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | Country code | `str3` | ISO / WDI 3-letter, uppercase | Not allowed | e.g. `AGO`, `ETH` |
| `year` | Survey year | `int` | 1990–2035 | Not allowed | Four-digit year of data collection |
| `survname` | Survey name | `str#` | — | Not allowed | Survey acronym (e.g. `GEIH`, `EHCVM`, `RHS`) |
| `hhid` | Household identifier | `str` | — | Not allowed | Unique per household within the survey; string to preserve leading zeros |
| `pid` | Person identifier | `str` | — | Not allowed | `hhid` and `pid` together must uniquely identify each row |
| `welfare` | Welfare aggregate (LCU, annual per capita) | `double` | > 0, LCU, annual per capita | Not allowed | Consumption or income aggregate from the survey's official poverty methodology  | 
| `welfare_self` | Self-reliance-adjusted welfare (LCU, annual per capita) | `double` | ≥ 0, LCU, annual per capita | Not allowed | Welfare net of humanitarian/social assistance, in the same units as `welfare`; must not exceed `welfare` in any row. Used for the 50by35 self-reliance indicator (see [Harmonize Data](02-harmonization.qmd)) |
| `welfare_type` | Welfare measure type | `byte` | `1`–`3` | Not allowed | `1` = Consumption, `2` = Income, `3` = Expenditure |
| `weight` | Sampling weight | `double` | > 0 | Not allowed | Individual sampling/population weight |
| `camp` | Camp/non-camp | `byte` | `0`/`1` | Allowed | `0` = Non-camp, `1` = Camp. The variable must exist, but may be missing in every row if the survey does not identify camp residence; it still needs the value label. Used for the camp breakdown of the indicators |
| `urban` | Urban/rural | `byte` | `0`/`1` | Allowed | `0` = Rural, `1` = Urban. The variable must exist, but may be missing in every row if the survey has no urban/rural split; it still needs the value label |

## Optional Variables

Optional variables may be left out of the file entirely. When included, individual rows may be missing (`.`) except for `natpovline`, which must have a value in every row.

| Variable | Label | Type | Unit / range | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hhsize` | Household size | `int` | ≥ 1 | Number of household members |
| `age` | Age (years) | `double` | 0–120 years | Decimal allowed for children under 5 (per GMD 2.0); integer otherwise |
| `male` | Sex | `byte` | `0`/`1` | `0` = Female, `1` = Male |
| `educat4` | Highest education (4 cat.) | `byte` | `1`–`4` | See value labels below |
| `empstat` | Employment status | `byte` | `1`–`4` | See value labels below |
| `strata` | Sampling strata | `int` | — | Design variable for variance estimation |
| `psu` | Primary sampling unit | `long` | — | Design variable for variance estimation |
| `natpovline` | National poverty line (LCU, annual per capita) | `double` | > 0, LCU, annual per capita | Express in the same currency, reference period, and price basis as `welfare` and `welfare_self`. If included, it must be non-missing in every row. When present, it is the line for the **primary** 50by35 self-reliance indicator |
| `arrival_year` | Year of arrival | `int` | 1900–survey year | Year the individual arrived in the host country |

## Value Labels

Categorical variables must use these codes and labels exactly.

`welfare_type`

: `1` Consumption · `2` Income · `3` Expenditure

`male`

: `0` Female · `1` Male

`camp`

: `0` Non-camp · `1` Camp

`urban`

: `0` Rural · `1` Urban

`educat4`

: `1` No education · `2` Primary · `3` Secondary · `4` Tertiary

`empstat`

: `1` Employed · `2` Unemployed · `3` Out of labor force · `4` Not applicable

## Validation

The validation scripts (`Stata/validate_50by35.do`, `R/validate_50by35.R`) run before every harmonized upload. An **error** stops the upload; a **warning** is printed and the upload continues.

| Result | What is checked |
|---|---|
| **Error** | All mandatory variables are present, with no missing values except `camp` and `urban`. |
| **Error** | `code` is a 3-letter uppercase string; `survname`, `hhid` and `pid` are non-empty strings; `hhid` + `pid` is unique. |
| **Error** | One survey per file: `code`, `year` and `survname` are constant across all rows. |
| **Error** | No extended missing values (`.a`–`.z`) in any numeric variable; use system missing (`.`). |
| **Error** | Ranges:`year` is an integer in 1990–2035; `welfare` and `weight` are > 0; `welfare_self` is ≥ 0 and ≤ `welfare`; `welfare_type` is 1–3; `camp` and `urban` are 0, 1 or missing. |
| **Error** | Categorical variables (`welfare_type`, `camp`, `urban`, and `male`, `educat4`, `empstat` when present) carry value labels with exactly the codes and text shown above: no extra and no missing codes. |
| **Error** | Optional variables, when present, are in range: `hhsize` is an integer ≥ 1; `age` is 0–120 and an integer from age 5; `male` is 0/1; `educat4` and `empstat` are 1–4; `strata` and `psu` are integers; `arrival_year` is an integer from 1900 to the survey year; `natpovline` is > 0 and non-missing in every row. |
| **Error** (Stata only) | Storage types: integer variables use `byte`/`int`/`long`, and real variables are not `float`. |
| **Warning** | `hhsize` differs from the number of `pid` records in the household. Rosters can be incomplete, and refugee-only samples keep a subset of household members. |
| **Warning** | A variable label differs from the **Label** column above. |

The validators do **not** check for numeric sentinel codes (e.g. `-9`, `99`) in variables without a range check (such as `strata` and `psu`), or the file name. These are still required: check them in your harmonization script.
